prompt:
Normalize the single contact record in the user’s note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. Each value must be a string or JSON null. No prose or Markdown.

1. Extract the record. Read only its Label<separator>value lines, allowing alternate labels, shuffled order, and colon, equals, or tab separators. Ignore surrounding notes and signatures. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent or empty values and these case-insensitive placeholders as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.
2. Assign before transforming. The country line supplies the explicit country. For the other lines, a value containing @ is email, regardless of label. A value with at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, or + - ( ) . / after stripping a leading tel: and a trailing extension is phone, regardless of label. Extensions include ext. or ext followed by digits, x followed by digits, # followed by digits, and extension followed by digits. If the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not, swap those values. Use the remaining name and company values according to their labels after this swap.
3. Resolve country and phone together. Convert the explicit country from an English, Swedish, or German name, alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, or common alias to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, case-insensitively. Aliases include UK and Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA and U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ. On the phone stripped of tel: and extension, detect international form by + or 00 at the start, ignoring an opening parenthesis. For an international phone, remove (0), strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and replace initial 00 with +. Keep its written calling code even if the country line disagrees. Only if the country is missing, use an international phone’s calling code to fill country when it identifies exactly one country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For a national phone, strip formatting punctuation and spaces, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalized country’s calling code. Without that country, a national phone is null. Output phones as E.164: + followed by digits only.
4. Normalize text. Name: split at the first comma if present and move the part after it before the part preceding it; remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, case-insensitively, with or without a dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. Company: remove one trailing legal suffix, and its optional preceding comma, case-insensitively, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. Legal suffixes for both steps: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Email: remove surrounding angle brackets and the mailto: prefix wherever they wrap the address, then lowercase. Trim the resulting values and collapse whitespace runs.
5. Check all five slots. Carry every assigned nonmissing value through its transformation; do not lose it because of its original label or unfamiliar surface form. Missing values are null except for the explicit international-phone country fallback above. Never use external note text, signatures, email domains, or company suffixes to fill or change another field.
